answerCheck.reason: The center (6,8) is the midpoint of the endpoints, each at center distance 10. The direct segment crosses the disk of radius 5. Each tangent portion has length sqrt(10^2-5^2)=5*sqrt(3). The angle at the center between a radius to a tangent point and the endpoint ray is arccos(1/2)=pi/3. The admissible joining minor arc therefore has angle pi-2*pi/3=pi/3 and length 5*pi/3. The two symmetric routes have equal length; the tangent-arc structure supplies the minimality proof.

routes.label: Construct a route and prove it is shortest

answerCheck.reason: The frustum has radii3 and 6 and height3*sqrt(3), so its slant height is 6. Extend the cone: similar axial triangles give inner and outer developed radii6 and 12. Cone unfolding gives a sector of angle pi because the outer circular rim has circumference12*pi; diametrically opposite generators therefore differ by pi/2 in the developed angle. The straight developed chord enters the removed radius-6 disk and is inadmissible. Here is a global lower bound without assuming a new shortest-path theorem. Any continuous surface path lifts to the annular cone development with endpoint angular difference pi/2+k*pi for an integer k; after reflection its absolute angular difference is at least pi/2. It must cross the ray at angle pi/3 from A=(12,0). At a first such point P=(r/2,sqrt(3)*r/2), r>=6, the coordinate-distance formula gives AP^2=(r-6)^2+108>=108. Thus the path before P has length at least6*sqrt(3). The remaining path has net angular travel at least pi/6 and stays outside the radius-6 disk. Radial projection to that circle cannot increase length: for unit vectors u,v and r,s>=6, the squared distance identity |r*u-s*v|^2=(r-s)^2+r*s*|u-v|^2>=36*|u-v|^2 proves contraction for every chord. Apply it to every ordered path partition and take the supremum defining curve length; the projected path must cover circular angular travel at least pi/6, of length at least pi by the arc formula. Hence every path has length at least6*sqrt(3)+pi, including paths that wind or cross a development seam. Attainment is a tangent segment from A to the inner circle at angle pi/3, length 6*sqrt(3), followed by the inner-rim arc of angle pi/6, length pi. It stays within the annulus. Therefore the shortest length is 6*sqrt(3)+pi, E.
